Typosquatted npm packages used to steal cloud and CI/CD secrets

Microsoft Security Blog
2026-05-29 18 use cases 5 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

The Mini Shai-Hulud campaign used malicious npm packages to target cloud and CI/CD credentials across developer environments. This report details the attack chain, detection opportunities, and mitigation guidance to help organizations identify and disrupt related activity. The post Typosquatted npm packages used to steal cloud and CI/CD secrets appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog .

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] vpmdhaj typosquat npm package install via preinstall hook (node child of npm) · [LLM] Bun runtime download from github.com/oven-sh during npm install (Gen-2 loader) · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Typosquatted npm packages used to steal cloud and CI/CD secrets
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] payload.bin written under node_modules by node process · [LLM] __DAEMONIZED=1 environment marker on spawned process · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound HTTP beacon to vpmdhaj C2 (aab.sportsontheweb.net) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Cloud metadata service hit (IMDSv2 / ECS) from node process under node_modules · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)
vpmdhaj typosquat npm package install via preinstall hook (node child of npm) AIDelivery High
Detects execution of the malicious vpmdhaj cluster of typosquat packages during npm install. Anchors on the exact package names published 2026-05-28 plus the preinstall/postinstall/install lifecycle hook tokens carried in the node command line. Rationale: Anchors on the exact package names and lifecycle-hook tokens documented in Microsoft's article (Block 1 in source) plus the Gen-1/Gen-2 stager filenames (preinstall.js, setup.mjs, opensearch_init.js, ai_init.js). Stagers run as a node child of npm during install — pairing process/parent narrows scope to the actual attack path, not generic npm telemetry.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal mirror that legitimately republishes a package whose name accidentally overlaps a victim string
  • Security researcher reproducing the campaign in a sandbox
  • Developer reading the article and pulling a hash-pinned copy for analysis
  • CI logs that echo package names from a dependency-tree dump that includes the strings as text
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--dry-run", "npm view", "npm search", "--json") and not ProcessCommandLine has_any ("preinstall.js", "setup.mjs", "payload.bin"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — pull the parent npm/yarn invocation, INIT_CWD, and the package-lock.json delta on the host; confirm a vpmdhaj-scoped or unscoped lookalike package was actually resolved (not just text in logs). 2) Contain — quarantine the host or runner, revoke any cloud / GitHub / npm tokens that lived in that environment after 2026-05-28T00:00Z, and blocklist the package names in the internal npm proxy. 3) Hunt — pivot on `payload.bin` writes under node_modules, outbound traffic to aab.sportsontheweb.net, and `__DAEMONIZED=1` env-tagged processes across the rest of the fleet.
DeviceProcessEvents

| where FileName in~ ("node.exe", "node", "npm.cmd", "npm.exe", "npx.cmd", "npx.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe", "node", "npm.cmd", "npm.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("preinstall", "postinstall", "npm install")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("preinstall", "postinstall", "npm install")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (
    "@vpmdhaj", "opensearch-setup", "opensearch-setup-tool",
    "opensearch-config-utility", "opensearch-security-scanner",
    "elastic-opensearch-helper", "search-engine-setup",
    "env-config-manager", "devops-tools", "search-setup", "elastic-helper",
    "preinstall.js", "setup.mjs", "opensearch_init.js", "ai_init.js"
  )
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (
    "@vpmdhaj", "opensearch-setup", "opensearch-setup-tool",
    "opensearch-config-utility", "opensearch-security-scanner",
    "elastic-opensearch-helper", "search-engine-setup",
    "env-config-manager", "devops-tools", "search-setup", "elastic-helper"
  )
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent

| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\\node.exe", "\\npm.cmd", "\\npx.cmd")
   or ParentProcessName has_any ("\\node.exe", "\\npm.cmd")
| where CommandLine has_any ("preinstall", "postinstall", "npm install")
| where CommandLine has_any (

payload.bin written under node_modules by node process AIInstallation High
Detects the Gen-1 stager dropping the ~195 KB Bun-compiled second-stage binary as payload.bin inside the package install directory beneath node_modules. The combination of filename, parent directory, and node initiating process is article-specific and very high fidelity. Rationale: Block 2 in the article literally is this detection — payload.bin name + node_modules path + node initiator is exactly the Gen-1 drop. Filename is too generic on its own (any backup or game asset could be called payload.bin) but combined with node_modules + node initiator the FP rate collapses.
ATT&CKT1105 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A legitimate npm package that ships its own file called payload.bin (uncommon but possible for asset-shipping libraries)
  • Developer manually copying a debug binary into node_modules during analysis
  • Build script that emits a file named payload.bin into a checked-out node_modules cache
  • Reproducing the campaign in a forensic sandbox
Suppression filter
| where not (FolderPath has_any ("\\@types\\", "\\.cache\\", "\\.bin\\") and FileSize < 1024)
Response runbook
1) Triage — hash the dropped payload.bin (Bun-compiled stage-2 should be ~195 KB single file) and pull the parent node command line for the originating package name. 2) Contain — kill the detached child if still running (`pgrep -af payload.bin` on Linux / Get-Process matching by ImageFileName on Windows), quarantine the file, and isolate the host or CI runner. 3) Hunt — across the fleet for the same SHA256 / size band, then pivot to outbound IMDS hits and aab.sportsontheweb.net DNS in the same host's history.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "payload.bin"
| where FolderPath has "node_modules"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe", "node", "npm.cmd", "npm.exe", "npx.cmd", "npx.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, FileSize, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType =~ "FileCreated"
| where TargetFileName =~ "payload.bin"
| where TargetFilePath has "node_modules"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node", "npm", "npx")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSize,
          TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Outbound HTTP beacon to vpmdhaj C2 (aab.sportsontheweb.net) AICommand & Control High
Detects the Gen-1 stager's HTTP C2 beacon and stage-2 download from the vpmdhaj-controlled domain. Scopes the connection on the C2 hostname plus node as the initiating process so non-developer traffic is excluded. Rationale: aab.sportsontheweb.net is the only IOC the article surfaces as a Gen-1 C2 host. Scoping on the FQDN (rather than the X-Supply header, which is not consistently captured in standard CEF / ASIM columns) gives a clean, high-fidelity detection that survives across DNS, proxy, and EDR network telemetry.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesWeb Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher resolving the domain for sinkhole / TI verification
  • Threat-intel feed crawler that resolves all IOCs from MSRC posts
  • Malware sandbox detonating the same package
  • Internal DNS resolver pre-fetching domains from a TI list
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe", "node", "npm.cmd", "npx.cmd") or isempty(InitiatingProcessFileName)
Response runbook
1) Triage — match the connection's initiating process: a `node` child of `npm install` is high-fidelity TP, a curl/researcher-tagged process is likely benign verification. Pull the X-Supply: 1 request header from the proxy if available — only the malware emits it. 2) Contain — sinkhole the FQDN at egress and DNS, block outbound to the resolved IP at the firewall, isolate the host or CI runner. 3) Hunt — cross-reference all hosts that resolved or connected to the FQDN in the last 30 days, and verify each one for `payload.bin` drops and `__DAEMONIZED=1` processes.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has "aab.sportsontheweb.net"
   or RemoteUrl endswith "sportsontheweb.net"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let C2Host = "aab.sportsontheweb.net";
(union isfuzzy=true
  (CommonSecurityLog
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
     | where DestinationHostName has C2Host
          or RequestURL has C2Host
          or DestinationDnsDomain has C2Host
     | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationHostName,
               RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, RequestMethod,
               SentBytes, ReceivedBytes, DeviceProduct),
  (ImWebSession
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
     | where Url has C2Host or DstHostname has C2Host
     | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstHostname,
               Url, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, HttpMethod,
               HttpRequestBodyBytes, HttpResponseBodyBytes, EventProduct),
  (DnsEvents
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
     | where Name has C2Host
     | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, ResultCode))
| order by TimeGenerated desc

__DAEMONIZED=1 environment marker on spawned process AIInstallation High
Detects the vpmdhaj stage-2 binary's self-re-entry guard, which sets __DAEMONIZED=1 in the environment of the detached child to avoid double-spawning. This env-var name is unique to this campaign per Microsoft's writeup. Rationale: Block 3 in the article — the __DAEMONIZED=1 string is a unique campaign artifact called out explicitly in Microsoft's writeup as the re-entry guard. The literal string is not a known legitimate environment variable in any common runtime so single-string match is sufficient.
ATT&CKT1543 T1564
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher re-detonating the sample in a sandbox
  • Internal copy of the campaign IOC list grepped at runtime by a SIEM-export job
  • Threat-intel blog ingested into a system that re-emits the string into a log line
Response runbook
1) Triage — locate the parent of the process bearing __DAEMONIZED=1 and trace back to the originating `npm install` or `setup.mjs`/`preinstall.js`. 2) Contain — kill the process, capture memory if forensics matters, then revoke any AWS / GitHub / Vault / npm tokens reachable from the host since the install. 3) Hunt — sweep the fleet for the same string and for the package-name set in UC1; assume every match is a confirmed stage-2 execution until proven otherwise.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "__DAEMONIZED=1"
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "__DAEMONIZED=1"
   or AdditionalFields has "__DAEMONIZED"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "__DAEMONIZED=1"
   or ParentProcessCommandLine has "__DAEMONIZED=1"
   or TargetProcessCommandLine has "__DAEMONIZED=1"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Cloud metadata service hit (IMDSv2 / ECS) from node process under node_modules AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the stage-2 credential harvester's queries against AWS Instance Metadata Service (169.254.169.254) and ECS task-role metadata (169.254.170.2) when the originating process is node — particularly when launched from a node_modules path. Pairs the EDR-side metadata fetch with the CloudTrail-side STS/SecretsManager fan-out for correlation. Rationale: 169.254.169.254 (IMDSv2) and 169.254.170.2 (ECS task role) are the exact metadata endpoints the article names. Pairing the link-local destination with a node/bun initiating process is the article-specific anchor; the CloudTrail companion query catches the fan-out across 16+ regions (GetCallerIdentity → AssumeRole → ListSecrets/GetSecretValue) called out as a defining behaviour of the stage-2 harvester.
ATT&CKT1552.005 T1528 T1555.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate AWS SDK call from a node app fetching role credentials on an EC2 instance or ECS task
  • Health check or sidecar agent polling IMDSv2 from a node container
  • Developer running the AWS CLI inside an EC2 dev box via a node-wrapper script
  • ECS exec / debug sessions where node tools probe the metadata endpoint
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "node_modules" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("preinstall.js", "setup.mjs", "opensearch_init.js", "ai_init.js", "payload.bin")
Response runbook
1) Triage — pull the InitiatingProcessFolderPath: any path under node_modules with a vpmdhaj-cluster package name is TP; a long-running app server is likely benign. Correlate to the CloudTrail query above on the same host's instance-role ARN. 2) Contain — revoke the instance/task role credentials (rotate role trust policy or detach the role), block egress to the C2 domain, isolate the host or task. 3) Hunt — pivot on the role ARN in CloudTrail for the previous 24h to spot follow-on activity (Secrets Manager reads, STS chained assumes, suspicious console logins from STS sessions), and check GitHub / npm token activity for the maintainer accounts that were on the host.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("169.254.169.254", "169.254.170.2")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe", "node", "bun.exe", "bun")
   or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "node_modules"
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("preinstall.js", "setup.mjs", "opensearch_init.js", "ai_init.js", "payload.bin")
| summarize HitCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            ParentCmds = make_set(InitiatingProcessCommandLine, 5),
            ParentPaths = make_set(InitiatingProcessFolderPath, 5)
            by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteIP
| order by FirstSeen desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in ("169.254.169.254", "169.254.170.2")
| where SrcUsername !endswith "$"
| summarize HitCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
          by DvcHostname, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, NetworkApplicationProtocol
| order by FirstSeen desc
title: AWS IMDSv2 / ECS Metadata Hit From Node
id: a7c91d54-2f8e-4b3a-9c1d-5e8f7a3b6c20
description: Detects an outbound connection to the AWS instance-metadata service (169.254.169.254) or ECS task-role metadata endpoint (169.254.170.2) initiated by a node / bun process — a signature of the vpmdhaj stage-2 credential harvester.
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/05/28/typosquatted-npm-packages-used-steal-cloud-ci-cd-secrets/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/29
tags:
  - attack.credential_access
  - attack.t1552.005
  - attack.t1555.006
logsource:
  category: network_connection
selection_ip:
  DestinationIp:
    - '169.254.169.254'
    - '169.254.170.2'
selection_proc:
  Image|endswith:
    - '\node.exe'
    - '\bun.exe'
    - '/node'
    - '/bun'
condition: selection_ip and selection_proc
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @DestinationIp:(169.254.169.254 OR 169.254.170.2) @Image:(*\node.exe OR *\bun.exe)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 RemoteAddressIP4=/^169\.254\.(169\.254|170\.2)$/
| ContextImageFileName=/(\\node\.exe|\\bun\.exe|\/node|\/bun)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemoteAddressIP4], function=count())
# log group: /aws/cloudtrail
fields @timestamp, eventName, eventSource, userIdentity.arn, userIdentity.type, userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer.userName, sourceIPAddress, userAgent, awsRegion
| filter eventName in ["GetCallerIdentity", "AssumeRole", "ListSecrets", "GetSecretValue"]
  and userIdentity.type in ["AssumedRole", "IAMUser", "WebIdentityUser"]
  and (userAgent like /aws-sdk-js/i or userAgent like /node/i or userAgent like /Bun/i)
| stats count() as call_count,
        count_distinct(eventName) as distinct_events,
        count_distinct(awsRegion) as distinct_regions,
        earliest(@timestamp) as first_seen,
        latest(@timestamp) as last_seen
        by userIdentity.arn, sourceIPAddress
| filter distinct_regions >= 5 and distinct_events >= 2
| sort call_count desc
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest IN ("169.254.169.254","169.254.170.2") AND All_Traffic.app="node") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.app All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest IN ("169.254.169.254","169.254.170.2") AND All_Traffic.app="node") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.app All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Bun runtime download from github.com/oven-sh during npm install (Gen-2 loader) AIDelivery Medium
Detects the Gen-2 stager's hallmark: an npm-driven node process fetching a legitimate Bun runtime release (v1.3.13) directly from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases as a loader for the bundled stage-2 payload. The combination of source (npm install) + destination (oven-sh/bun release asset) is the article-specific signal. Rationale: The article names github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases v1.3.13 as the legitimate-but-abused payload host for the Gen-2 setup.mjs loader. github.com is trusted egress so destination alone is too noisy; pairing it with a node/npm initiating process during install lifecycle bounds the FP rate to actual Bun adopters.
ATT&CKT1105 T1218
Data sourcesWeb Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Development team genuinely adopting Bun and downloading it through a postinstall in their own package
  • CI workflow that bootstraps Bun via npm in a build job
  • Devcontainer / Dockerfile that pulls Bun for runtime tooling
  • Reproducing the article in a sandbox
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("setup.mjs", "opensearch_init.js", "ai_init.js") or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "node_modules"
Response runbook
1) Triage — pull the parent npm package name from the InitiatingProcess chain; if it matches the vpmdhaj cluster or is a recently published unsigned package, treat as TP. Otherwise verify Bun is on the team's known-tools list. 2) Contain — quarantine the downloaded bun binary, kill any setup.mjs / opensearch_init.js / ai_init.js processes, isolate the host or runner. 3) Hunt — sweep the fleet for nodes that fetched bun/releases in the last 90 days and correlate with payload.bin drops, __DAEMONIZED markers, and IMDS hits.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has "github.com" and RemoteUrl has "oven-sh/bun"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe", "node", "npm.cmd", "npm.exe", "npx.cmd")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node.exe", "node", "npm.cmd", "npm.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("setup.mjs", "preinstall", "postinstall", "npm install", "node_modules")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Url has "github.com" and Url has "oven-sh/bun"
| join kind=inner (
    ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("node", "npm", "npx")
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("setup.mjs", "preinstall", "postinstall", "npm install", "node_modules")
  ) on $left.DvcHostname == $right.DvcHostname
| where abs(datetime_diff('second', TimeGenerated, TimeGenerated1)) <= 300
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, Url, DstHostname,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Bun Runtime Pulled From GitHub During npm Install
id: 4f1c9a23-8b5d-4e62-aa31-7c2f5d8e9b14
description: Detects the Gen-2 vpmdhaj loader fetching the legitimate Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases as a bring-your-own loader for the bundled stage-2 payload during npm install.
references:

level: medium

#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/github\.com/i ContextImageFileName=/(\\node\.exe|\\npm\.cmd|\/node|\/npm)$/i

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web where (Web.url="*github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases*" AND Web.app IN ("node","node.exe","npm","npm.cmd")) by Web.src Web.user Web.dest Web.url Web.app | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web where (Web.url="*github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases*" AND Web.app IN ("node","node.exe","npm","npm.cmd")) by Web.src Web.user Web.dest Web.url Web.app | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

MDM tools like Jamf and Kandji are essential but they don't see npm installs, IDE extensions, or AI coding tools. Here's what's actually unprotected on your developer machines and how to close the gap. Category: Guides & Best Practices

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Shai-Hulud worm GitHub Action workflow file dropped under .github/workflows · [LLM] npm/yarn/pnpm postinstall hook spawning credential-harvest tooling · Suspicious browser extension installation · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Cyberhaven trojanized Chrome extension C2 callback to cyberhavenext.pro · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud npm worm exfil to filev2.getsession.org · [LLM] postmark-mcp BCC exfil to giftshop.club · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Cyberhaven trojanized Chrome extension C2 callback to cyberhavenext.pro AICommand & Control High
Hunts for DNS/HTTPS resolution to cyberhavenext.pro from Chromium-based browsers — the C2 domain used by the malicious Cyberhaven Chrome extension (v24.10.4, active 25–26 Dec 2024) and ~35 related extensions in the Secure Annex cluster. The extension's worker.js fetched its config from this host before exfiltrating cookies and authenticated sessions. Rationale: Article names cyberhavenext.pro as an explicit IOC. Cross-checked against Cyberhaven's own engineering blog, Secure Annex's cluster analysis, Darktrace and Obsidian Security write-ups — all confirm the domain as the C2 used by the malicious worker.js bundled in extension v24.10.4 to retrieve config before stealing cookies/auth sessions. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cyberhaven.com/engineering-blog/cyberhavens-preliminary-analysis-of-the-recent-malicious-chrome-extension • https://secureannex.com/blog/cyberhaven-extension-compromise/ • https://www.darktrace.com/blog/cyberhaven-supply-chain-attack-exploiting-browser-extensions • https://www.obsidiansecurity.com/resource/behind-the-breach-malicious-attack-on-cyberhavens-chrome-extension-developer-team
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1176 T1539
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal threat-intel feed validation / VirusTotal-style hash lookups that resolve the domain
  • Security researcher sandbox detonation traffic
  • DNS sinkhole logging the domain after redirection
  • Backup/cache entries causing repeat resolution after EDR cleanup
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("smartscreen.exe","mpcmdrun.exe") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "sandbox"
Response runbook
Triage: pull the InitiatingProcessFileName — confirm chrome/edge/brave parent and the Chrome extension ID via DeviceFileEvents under \Extensions\pajkjnmeojmbapicmbpliphjmcekeaac\ (or other IDs in the Secure Annex cluster). Identify the signed-in user and what SaaS sessions they had open. Contain: revoke all active browser/SSO sessions for the user (Okta sessions, Entra continuous access), force-rotate any cookies/tokens in the browser profile, and quarantine the host. Hunt: scope to any device that has DeviceFileEvents under the Cyberhaven extension folder for ActionType FileCreated between 25–26 Dec 2024 OR has ever resolved cyberhavenext.pro; also enumerate other IDs from the Secure Annex cluster on the same host's extension folder.
let IOC = dynamic(["cyberhavenext.pro"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (IOC)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let IOC = dynamic(["cyberhavenext.pro"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImDnsActivity | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DnsQuery has_any (IOC) | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, DstIpAddr=DvcIpAddr),
  (ImWebSession | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where Url has_any (IOC) or DstHostname has_any (IOC) | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername=SrcUsername, Url, DstIpAddr)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Mini Shai-Hulud npm worm exfil to filev2.getsession.org AIActions on Objectives High
Detects outbound traffic to filev2.getsession.org — the Session decentralised-network endpoint the Mini Shai-Hulud / Sha1-Hulud npm worm uses to exfil harvested GitHub, npm, cloud, Kubernetes, Vault, Docker and SSH credentials. Scopes to Node.js / package-manager process context so it doesn't fire on a real user running the Session messenger. Rationale: Article lists filev2.getsession.org in the IOC bundle. Cross-checked with Wiz (Mini Shai-Hulud), Socket (Tanstack packages), BleepingComputer and StepSecurity — all confirm Session's decentralized P2P file API as the exfil channel; gating on Node/npm/yarn/pnpm/bun parent process distinguishes worm exfil from a real user's Session messenger traffic. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-strikes-again-tanstack-more-npm-packages-compromised • https://socket.dev/blog/tanstack-npm-packages-compromised-mini-shai-hulud-supply-chain-attack • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-is-back-a-self-spreading-supply-chain-attack-hits-the-npm-ecosystem • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/new-shai-hulud-malware-wave-compromises-600-npm-packages/
ATT&CKT1567 T1195.002 T1552.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer running the actual Session desktop client (Session.exe parent, not node.exe)
  • Penetration tester replaying the Mini Shai-Hulud sample in a sandbox
  • Researcher running TruffleHog inside an npm script for legitimate secret scanning
  • Network appliance health-check probes to popular hostnames
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("session.exe","session-desktop.exe") and InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("session.exe","session-desktop.exe")
Response runbook
Triage: pull the full InitiatingProcessCommandLine and walk back to the npm/yarn install that ran — capture which package name and version was being installed (lock file diff). Pull ~/.npmrc, ~/.gitconfig, AWS/Azure CLI creds, GH PATs the worm targets. Contain: revoke and rotate every credential exposed on the host (npm publish tokens, GH PATs, AWS keys, kubeconfig, Vault tokens), block filev2.getsession.org egress, and quarantine the device. Hunt: query for any host that wrote .github/workflows/shai-hulud-workflow.yml or pushed a branch matching shai-hulud-*, and any github.com push from non-CI IPs in the last 7 days; pivot on the publisher username of the compromised package to find related installs.
let PkgMgrs = dynamic(["node.exe","npm.exe","npm.cmd","npx.exe","npx.cmd","yarn.exe","yarn.cmd","pnpm.exe","pnpm.cmd","bun.exe","node","npm","yarn","pnpm","bun","curl.exe","wget.exe"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has "filev2.getsession.org" or RemoteUrl has "getsession.org"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (PkgMgrs)
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ (PkgMgrs)
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("setup_bun.js","bun_environment.js","node_modules")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let PkgMgrs = dynamic(["node.exe","npm.exe","npm.cmd","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","bun.exe","node","npm","yarn","pnpm","bun","curl.exe","wget.exe"]);
let IOC = dynamic(["filev2.getsession.org","getsession.org"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImDnsActivity | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DnsQuery has_any (IOC) | extend Actor=SrcUsername, Host=DvcHostname, Cmdline="", DstUrl=DnsQuery),
  (ImNetworkSession | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DstHostname has_any (IOC) or Url has_any (IOC) | extend Actor=SrcUsername, Host=DvcHostname, Cmdline="", DstUrl=coalesce(Url, DstHostname)),
  (ImWebSession | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where Url has_any (IOC) | extend Actor=SrcUsername, Host=DvcHostname, Cmdline="", DstUrl=Url)
| project TimeGenerated, Host, Actor, DstUrl
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Shai-Hulud worm GitHub Action workflow file dropped under .github/workflows AIInstallation High
Detects file creation of shai-hulud-workflow.yml / shai-hulud.yaml / discussion.yaml under any .github/workflows/ directory on a developer host. The Shai-Hulud and Shai-Hulud 2.0 worms write this workflow then push it to a fresh branch so a PUSH-triggered Action exfiltrates harvested secrets. Rationale: Article references Mini Shai-Hulud and the postinstall credential-theft chain. Workflow filename triplet (shai-hulud-workflow.yml / shai-hulud.yaml / discussion.yaml) confirmed by Unit 42, Wiz, Datadog Security Labs and their public IOC repo. File-creation telemetry catches the worm during install-time, well before its GitHub push step. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/npm-supply-chain-attack/ • https://www.wiz.io/blog/shai-hulud-npm-supply-chain-attack • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/shai-hulud-2.0-npm-worm/ • https://github.com/DataDog/indicators-of-compromise/tree/main/shai-hulud-2.0 • https://research.jfrog.com/post/shai-hulud-here-we-go-again/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1546 T1567.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat researcher reproducing the worm in a contained lab repo
  • Red team / purple team retesting a previous Shai-Hulud incident
  • Backup software restoring an old repo snapshot that contained the file
  • Detection-engineering test ingesting public IOC samples
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("sandbox","test-shai-hulud","ioc-repo") or DeviceName has_any ("sandbox-","detlab-","redteam-"))
Response runbook
Triage: dump the file SHA256 and the InitiatingProcessCommandLine — confirm parent is npm/yarn/pnpm/node and capture which package install triggered it. Pull the workflow YAML content to confirm it matches the worm template (push trigger + curl/base64 exfil block). Contain: kill the install process tree, delete the workflow file, revoke any GH PAT or npm token that the parent npm session had access to, and rotate cloud creds harvested by the worm payload. Hunt: query DeviceNetworkEvents on the same host for filev2.getsession.org or webhook.site over the past 24h; enumerate every other host that installed the same compromised package@version (npm cache, lockfile pushes); audit GitHub for any branch named shai-hulud-* or any new public repo named Shai-Hulud / matching 'Sha1-Hulud: The Second Coming' description.
let WormFiles = dynamic(["shai-hulud-workflow.yml","shai-hulud.yaml","shai-hulud.yml","discussion.yaml","discussion.yml"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FileName in~ (WormFiles)
| where FolderPath has @"\.github\workflows" or FolderPath has "/.github/workflows"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let WormFiles = dynamic(["shai-hulud-workflow.yml","shai-hulud.yaml","shai-hulud.yml","discussion.yaml","discussion.yml"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFileName in~ (WormFiles)
| where TargetFilePath has @"\.github\workflows" or TargetFilePath has "/.github/workflows"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

postmark-mcp BCC exfil to giftshop.club AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts for outbound DNS/HTTPS to giftshop.club — the domain hosting phan@giftshop.club, the BCC recipient hard-coded into postmark-mcp v1.0.16 (the first publicly documented malicious npm-distributed MCP server, disclosed by Koi Security). Also catches BCC of organisational email to @giftshop.club via mail-flow telemetry. Rationale: Article lists giftshop.club in the IOC bundle. Koi Security (original disclosure), Snyk, BleepingComputer and the official Postmark advisory all confirm the BCC address phan@giftshop.club embedded in postmark-mcp v1.0.16. Detecting on the domain catches both the BCC mail leg (via Office mail-flow) and any local Node.js process resolving it during MCP server startup. Cross-checked against: • https://www.koi.ai/blog/postmark-mcp-npm-malicious-backdoor-email-theft • https://snyk.io/blog/malicious-mcp-server-on-npm-postmark-mcp-harvests-emails/ • https://postmarkapp.com/blog/information-regarding-malicious-postmark-mcp-package • https://thehackernews.com/2025/09/first-malicious-mcp-server-found.html

| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("smartscreen.exe","mpcmdrun.exe","defendersmartscreen.exe")
Response runbook
Triage: identify the AI assistant / MCP client invoking postmark-mcp (Cursor, Claude Code, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot Extensions) and the developer whose mailbox is integrated. Pull EmailEvents for the past 90 days to enumerate every message the MCP server sent and would have BCC'd. Contain: kill the MCP server process, uninstall postmark-mcp from every developer host (npm/pnpm/yarn ls -g and project node_modules), rotate the Postmark server token and any other credentials referenced in sent emails. Hunt: pivot on npm publisher 'phanpak' to identify the 31 other packages by the same author; query for any developer host that resolved giftshop.club or installed any package from publisher=phanpak in the last 6 months; review the affected mailbox for sensitive content the attacker now has copies of.
let IOC = dynamic(["giftshop.club"]);
let Net = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where RemoteUrl has_any (IOC)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Actor=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Process=InitiatingProcessFileName, Cmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Indicator=RemoteUrl, Path="network";
let Mail = EmailEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where RecipientEmailAddress has_any (IOC) or SenderFromAddress has_any (IOC)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName="", Actor=SenderFromAddress, Process="", Cmd=Subject, Indicator=RecipientEmailAddress, Path="mail";
union Net, Mail
| order by Timestamp desc
let IOC = dynamic(["giftshop.club"]);
let Net = union isfuzzy=true
    (ImDnsActivity | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DnsQuery has_any (IOC) | project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, Actor=SrcUsername, Indicator=DnsQuery, Path="dns"),
    (ImWebSession | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where Url has_any (IOC) or DstHostname has_any (IOC) | project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, Actor=SrcUsername, Indicator=coalesce(Url,DstHostname), Path="web");
let Mail = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Operation in ("Send","SendOnBehalf","SendAs") and (Recipients has "giftshop.club" or P2RecipientList has "giftshop.club" or P2Sender has "giftshop.club")
    | project TimeGenerated, Host="", Actor=UserId, Indicator=tostring(Recipients), Path="mail";
union Net, Mail
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: postmark-mcp Malicious MCP Server Exfil Domain (giftshop.club)
id: 9b6e3c02-7d5a-4e28-8f94-3b8f9c0d5e23
description: DNS query to giftshop.club — the attacker domain hosting phan@giftshop.club, the BCC recipient hard-coded into postmark-mcp npm v1.0.16, the first publicly documented malicious MCP server (disclosed by Koi Security, Sep 2025).

(source:windows.sysmon OR source:windows.defender OR source:linux.auditd OR source:cloudtrail) (@DomainName:(*giftshop.club* OR *GIFTSHOP.CLUB*) OR @DestinationHostname:(*giftshop.club* OR *GIFTSHOP.CLUB*) OR @RemoteUrl:(*giftshop.club*) OR @evt.outcome:success @network.destination.domain:*giftshop.club*)

npm/yarn/pnpm postinstall hook spawning credential-harvest tooling AIInstallation Medium
Hunts for package-manager processes (npm/npx/yarn/pnpm/node/bun) spawning TruffleHog, curl/wget reaching the Shai-Hulud or postmark-mcp exfil hosts, or executing setup_bun.js / bun_environment.js — the signature install-time payload chain used by the Mini Shai-Hulud and Shai-Hulud 2.0 worms before EDR has a behavioural signal to bite on. Rationale: Article describes the npm postinstall credential-scraping chain (Mini Shai-Hulud, postmark-mcp). Datadog IOC repo, Wiz, Socket and Sysdig confirm setup_bun.js / bun_environment.js and TruffleHog binary execution from npm contexts as the post-compromise install-time signal — plus the webhook.site / filev2.getsession.org / giftshop.club exfil strings catch curl/wget invocations the worm chains. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-strikes-again-tanstack-more-npm-packages-compromised • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/shai-hulud-2.0-npm-worm/ • https://socket.dev/blog/tanstack-npm-packages-compromised-mini-shai-hulud-supply-chain-attack • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/shai-hulud-the-novel-self-replicating-worm-infecting-hundreds-of-npm-packages • https://github.com/DataDog/indicators-of-compromise/tree/main/shai-hulud-2.0
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1195.002 T1552.001 T1546.016
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • CI/CD runners executing TruffleHog inside an npm script for legitimate secret scanning (e.g. GitHub Actions secret-scan job)
  • Developer using a Node-based wrapper around TruffleHog for repo audits
  • Build tooling that downloads bun via setup-bun in a controlled installer
  • Husky / lefthook pre-commit hooks running curl against internal services
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("buildkite-agent.exe","runner.exe","actions-runner.exe","jenkins.exe") or DeviceName has_any ("ci-","build-","runner-","github-actions-"))
Response runbook
Triage: capture full process tree (parent npm command → child) and the originating package name from npm's debug log (npm-debug.log / pnpm-debug.log / yarn-error.log). Confirm whether the executing npm install was kicked off by the developer or by a watch process. Contain: kill the install tree, roll back npm install in the project, and apply ignore-scripts=true in the user's .npmrc as a temporary hard-stop. Rotate any credentials the parent shell had in environment variables or files in ~/.config, ~/.aws, ~/.kube, ~/.npmrc, ~/.gitconfig. Hunt: query DeviceNetworkEvents on the host for filev2.getsession.org / giftshop.club / webhook.site / cyberhavenext.pro over the last 30 days; cross-ref every host that installed the same package@version from the lockfile diff; pivot on npm publisher to flag related malicious packages.
let PkgMgrs = dynamic(["npm.exe","npm.cmd","npx.exe","npx.cmd","yarn.exe","yarn.cmd","pnpm.exe","pnpm.cmd","node.exe","bun.exe","npm","npx","node","yarn","pnpm","bun"]);
let SuspChildren = dynamic(["trufflehog.exe","trufflehog","curl.exe","wget.exe","bun.exe"]);
let SuspStrings = dynamic(["setup_bun.js","bun_environment.js","trufflehog","webhook.site","filev2.getsession.org","giftshop.club"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (PkgMgrs)
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ (PkgMgrs)
| where FileName in~ (SuspChildren)
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any (SuspStrings)
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (SuspStrings)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let PkgMgrs = dynamic(["npm.exe","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","node.exe","bun.exe","npm","npx","node","yarn","pnpm","bun"]);
let SuspChildren = dynamic(["trufflehog.exe","trufflehog","curl.exe","wget.exe","bun.exe"]);
let SuspStrings = dynamic(["setup_bun.js","bun_environment.js","trufflehog","webhook.site","filev2.getsession.org","giftshop.club"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any (PkgMgrs) or ActingProcessName has_any (PkgMgrs)
| where TargetProcessName has_any (SuspChildren) or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (SuspStrings) or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (SuspStrings)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Package-Manager Postinstall Hook Spawning Credential-Harvest Tooling
id: a1c7f4b3-8e6c-4f39-9a5b-4c9d0e1f6234
description: npm/npx/yarn/pnpm/node/bun spawning trufflehog, or executing setup_bun.js / bun_environment.js, or reaching Shai-Hulud / postmark-mcp exfil hosts — the install-time payload chain documented across the Mini Shai-Hulud and Shai-Hulud 2.0 npm worm waves.
references:
  - https://www.wiz.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-strikes-again-tanstack-more-npm-packages-compromised
  - https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/shai-hulud-2.0-npm-worm/
  - https://socket.dev/blog/tanstack-npm-packages-compromised-mini-shai-hulud-supply-chain-attack
  - https://www.koi.ai/blog/postmark-mcp-npm-malicious-backdoor-email-theft
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/28
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.007
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1552.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  parent_pkg_mgr:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '\npx.exe'
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\yarn.exe'
      - '\pnpm.exe'
      - '\bun.exe'
      - '/npm'
      - '/npx'
      - '/node'
      - '/yarn'
      - '/pnpm'
      - '/bun'
  child_susp_tool:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\trufflehog.exe'
      - '\trufflehog'
      - '/trufflehog'
      - '\bun.exe'
  child_susp_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'setup_bun.js'
      - 'bun_environment.js'
      - 'trufflehog'
      - 'webhook.site'
      - 'filev2.getsession.org'
      - 'giftshop.club'
  condition: parent_pkg_mgr and (child_susp_tool or child_susp_cmd)
falsepositives:
  - CI/CD pipelines that legitimately run trufflehog secret scanning inside npm scripts
  - Developers manually invoking trufflehog from a Node tool wrapper
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\npm.exe OR *\Npm.exe OR *\npx.exe OR *\node.exe OR *\Node.exe OR *\yarn.exe OR *\pnpm.exe OR *\bun.exe) (@Image:(*\trufflehog.exe OR *\TruffleHog.exe OR *\curl.exe OR *\wget.exe OR *\bun.exe) OR @CommandLine:(*setup_bun.js* OR *bun_environment.js* OR *trufflehog* OR *TruffleHog* OR *webhook.site* OR *filev2.getsession.org* OR *giftshop.club*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^(npm|npx|node|yarn|pnpm|bun)(\.exe)?$/i
| ImageFileName=/(trufflehog|curl|wget|bun)(\.exe)?$/i OR CommandLine=/(setup_bun\.js|bun_environment\.js|trufflehog|webhook\.site|filev2\.getsession\.org|giftshop\.club)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("npm.exe","npx.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","bun.exe","npm","npx","node","yarn","pnpm","bun")) AND (Processes.process_name IN ("trufflehog.exe","trufflehog","curl.exe","wget.exe","bun.exe") OR Processes.process="*setup_bun.js*" OR Processes.process="*bun_environment.js*" OR Processes.process="*trufflehog*" OR Processes.process="*webhook.site*" OR Processes.process="*filev2.getsession.org*" OR Processes.process="*giftshop.club*") by host Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("npm.exe","npx.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","bun.exe","npm","npx","node","yarn","pnpm","bun")) AND (Processes.process_name IN ("trufflehog.exe","trufflehog","curl.exe","wget.exe","bun.exe") OR Processes.process="*setup_bun.js*" OR Processes.process="*bun_environment.js*" OR Processes.process="*trufflehog*" OR Processes.process="*webhook.site*" OR Processes.process="*filev2.getsession.org*" OR Processes.process="*giftshop.club*") by host Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("") or RemoteUrl has_any ("cyberhavenext.pro", "giftshop.club", "filev2.getsession.org")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic([""]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["cyberhavenext.pro", "giftshop.club", "filev2.getsession.org"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Suspicious browser extension installation Installation Medium

ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"

| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

ImFileEvent

                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",

| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
